relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with genetically confirmed arterial tortuosity syndrome: "the baby was found to have homozygous mutation in c.243C > G p.(Ser81Arg) in the SLC2A10 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). Two in-scope people: the case-report patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and her brother ('brother of patient', rule 2), who has a 'genetically confirmed diagnosis of arterial tortuosity syndrome' but no printed variant and no stated gene, so he has no variants row; consanguinity 'yes' recorded for him because the paper states the patient's parents (his parents too) are consanguineous. No tables. Patient's checklist: 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' left not reported although the 2-month exam states 'no respiratory distress', because she had tachypnea at 1 hour of age treated with oxygen and later needed HFNC respiratory support in intensive care for bronchiolitis (time-varying, conflicting evidence); the excluded feature row is kept with its time context. 'Mildly tortuous great vessels with no obstruction' was not used to exclude pulmonary artery stenosis or aortic/aortic-branch stenosis (great vessels not named; narrow/broad rule). 'No other cardiac defect' was not used to exclude ventricular hypertrophy (too general). 'Appropriate for gestational age' not recorded as a feature. Age at last evaluation taken as the follow-up CT at 43 months; the text also says follow-up continued 'for the following 4 years'. Age at diagnosis not stated. Cervical lung hernia onset recorded as 2 months (when the mother reported the neck lump), although the authors call it congenital. Variant type, inheritance and pathogenicity are not stated (the paper does not call c.243C > G missense). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (paper is silent). No contradictions found.
